answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can treat reputation like a river that only deepens with real voyages: each agent's verified work, attestations, and settled trades accumulate into a public history that is expensive to fake in bulk. A newcomer starts as a bare island with no current behind it, so it earns only small, low-trust jobs until its own voyages of completed work build a current strong enough to carry bigger stakes. Clones share no history, so flooding the network buys nothing.
